notes: Account summary: Aerodyne LatencyCraft builds automated market-making and risk models that must make decisions in 5-20ms on small inputs. Highly cost-conscious because model calls scale with market ticks.

Primary ask: POC to prove latency SLOs while showing cost per 1M calls under expected workload. Interested in Redwood strategies: batching windows, prefix/KV caching for repeated context, and aggressive quantization (4-bit/8-bit) if quality holds.
From discovery: 'if p95 goes above 30ms we lose production viability' – infra lead. Emphasis on consistent p95 not just p50.

Workload profile: many tiny requests (avg tokens 12–40) for trading logic + occasional larger embedding/rerank jobs for offline models. Mixed qps: baseline 500 rps with spikes to 3k rps during open hours.

Perf POC acceptance criteria (agreed): p50 < 8ms for short-gen path, p95 < 30ms; embedding latency < 80ms p95; throughput sustain at 3k rps for 1 minute without queue growth; end-to-end cost model showing <= $X per 100k short-gen calls (Redwood to propose values).

Technical constraints: must run inside customer VPC for order books, HSM-backed KMS for signing, audit logs retained 1 year. Air-gapped not required but on_prem option desirable for future compliance.

Quantization note: willing to test int8 and 4-bit QAT variants; will provide labeled evaluation prompts for quality regression checks. Keen to see Redwood Optimize recommendations (per-model quant profiles).

Benchmark ask: Redwood to run baseline perf against 3 model variants (small autoreg model ~1–3B, mid 7–13B int8, and a 13–30B 4-bit) with both dynamic batching and forced micro-batching; include cold-start vs warmed-KV results and cache hit-rate sensitivity.
Potential blockers: their procurement needs a clear SLA + price cap; security team needs encryption-in-transit proof and SOC2 report before Dedicated contract.
